#Task 2

```{r}
colSums(is.na(iris))

iris_clean=na.omit(iris)

sum(duplicated(iris_clean))

iris_clean=iris_clean%>%distinct()

str(iris_clean)

iris_clean$Species <- as.factor(iris_clean$Species)

summary(iris_clean)

cat("Number of Rows:", nrow(iris_clean), "\n")
cat("Number of Columns:", ncol(iris_clean), "\n")

cat("\nKey Insights:\n")
cat("1. No missing values were found in the Iris dataset.\n")
cat("2. Duplicate records were checked and removed if present.\n")
cat("3. Data types were verified and formatted correctly.\n")
cat("4. The dataset is now clean and ready for analysis.\n")

cat("\nKey Skills Used:\n")
cat("• Data Preprocessing\n")
cat("• Data Cleaning\n")
cat("• Data Quality Management\n")
cat("• Missing Value Handling\n")

```

#Task 3
```{r}

colMeans(iris[,1:4])

apply(iris[,1:4], 2, median)

apply(iris[,1:4], 2, sd)

table(iris$Species)

library(ggplot2)
# Sepal Length Distribution
ggplot(iris, aes(x = Sepal.Length, fill = Species)) +
  geom_histogram(binwidth = 0.3) +
  ggtitle("Distribution of Sepal Length")

# Petal Length vs Petal Width
ggplot(iris, aes(x = Petal.Length,
                 y = Petal.Width,
                 color = Species)) +
  geom_point(size = 3) +
  ggtitle("Petal Length vs Petal Width")

# Boxplot for Outlier Detection
ggplot(iris, aes(x = Species,
                 y = Sepal.Width,
                 fill = Species)) +
  geom_boxplot() +
  ggtitle("Boxplot of Sepal Width")

#Correlation Analysis

cor(iris[,1:4])

#Outlier Detection

boxplot(iris$Sepal.Length,
        main = "Outlier Detection for Sepal Length")

cat("Key Findings:\n")

cat("1. Petal Length and Petal Width show strong positive correlation.\n")

cat("2. Setosa species is clearly separated from other species.\n")

cat("3. Some outliers are present in Sepal Width.\n")

cat("4. Most flower measurements follow a consistent distribution.\n")

cat("\nKey Skills Used:\n")

cat("• Statistical Thinking\n")
cat("• Data Analysis\n")
cat("• Exploratory Data Analysis (EDA)\n")
cat("• Trend and Outlier Identification\n")
```

#task 5

```{r}
library(caret)
set.seed(123)

train_index <- createDataPartition(iris$Species,
                                   p = 0.7,
                                   list = FALSE)

train_data <- iris[train_index, ]
test_data <- iris[-train_index, ]

library(rpart)

model <- rpart(Species ~ .,
               data = train_data,
               method = "class")

# View Model
print(model)

predictions <- predict(model,
                       test_data,
                       type = "class")

confusionMatrix(predictions,
                test_data$Species)

ggplot(iris,
       aes(x = Petal.Length,
           y = Petal.Width,
           color = Species)) +
  geom_point(size = 3) +
  ggtitle("Species Classification using Petal Features")

cat("Key Insights:\n")

cat("1. Classification models help predict flower species based on measurements.\n")

cat("2. Petal Length and Petal Width are important predictors.\n")

cat("3. Setosa species is easily distinguishable from others.\n")

cat("4. Machine learning improves pattern recognition and prediction accuracy.\n")

cat("\nConclusion:\n")

cat("The classification model was successfully developed using the Iris dataset.\n")

cat("The model predicts flower species using sepal and petal measurements.\n")

cat("This task demonstrates the application of basic machine learning concepts for predictive analysis.\n")

cat("\nKey Skills Used:\n")

cat("• Basic Machine Learning Concepts\n")
cat("• Classification Modeling\n")
cat("• Model Understanding\n")
cat("• Predictive Analysis\n")
```
